articleTitle: Colloquium on Understanding your condition monitoring
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Understanding your Condition Monitoring (Ref. No.1999/117)
IEE Colloquium on Understanding your Condition Monitoring (Ref. No.1999/117)
abstract: Vibration monitoring is the most reliable method of assessing the overall health, or changes in health, of a rotor system. It has in the past been used to avert some catastrophic failures. In order to benefit fully from a vibration monitoring system it is important to appreciate what vibration is, how it is measured, how vibration measurements are presented and what can be learned from each presentation format. Typical vibration characteristics of a generator rotor are described together with measurement techniques and transducers. Vibration data presentation in several typical formats are described showing how one format can complement another. International standards of evaluation used to determine the acceptability of vibration are presented. Finally, future trends in vibration monitoring are briefly discussed and the requirements for an automated system outlined.

articleTitle: Current low power core testing using EL CID
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Understanding your Condition Monitoring (Ref. No.1999/117)
abstract: Traditional test methods to provide information on the condition of insulation between core laminations of large rotating electrical machines require a substantial supply to excite the core at rated magnetic flux, temperature rises due to faults being detected by various means. The test is performed with the rotor removed utilising significant time and labour. Increasing use is now made by manufacturers and utilities of the alternative low flux EL CID (electromagnetic core imperfection detector) test. With low excitation power, faults are detected electromagnetically with the ability to detect faults behind windings. Taking much less time than the rated flux test, and with reduced safety constraints, it may be the only test option practicable in an outage. In some instances tests may be made without removal of the rotor, not feasible with a high power test. An outline of the theoretical and practical considerations for EL CID testing are discussed. EL CID is applicable to both turbogenerators and hydrogenerators, differences are mainly confirmed to test implementation and interpretation of spurious effects.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Understanding your Condition Monitoring (Ref. No.1999/117)
abstract: The paper describes the Siemens' (formerly Parsons') Rotor Shorted Turn Monitor (RSTM). The monitor was developed in the early 1990s for application to large steam turbine driven generator rotors. At the heart of the RSTM is a mathematical algorithm which processes the signal from a search coil located in the air-gap. This analysis program is called in sequence for 1 to 4 generators by a supervisory program which records the results and presents them, in a variety of forms, to a PC screen. Many results were collected from one of the first RSTMs to be placed in service at a UK power station having rotors with a history of shorted turn indications. From these it was possible to assess the effectiveness on the analysis program in coping with the influence of magnetic saturation in the rotor teeth over a wide range of load. The paper also outlines alternative methods for detecting shorted turns, their causes and the case for continuous monitoring.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Understanding your Condition Monitoring (Ref. No.1999/117)
abstract: The analysis of rotor vibration monitoring is essentially a process of pattern recognition in the changes of bearing vibrations during normal operation and under test conditions. The probable cause of any change can usually be identified in general terms although the exact cause is rarely predicted without a physical investigation of the rotor. Nevertheless, such analysis can predict some types of shaft integrity problems and has prevented catastrophic failure in the past. The paper describes the vibration changes which are characteristics of typical balance problems which occur in turbine generators. Simple mechanical unbalance, thermal unbalance, rubbing effects, nonsynchronous vibrations, and shaft integrity are covered.

articleTitle: Condition monitoring of HV electrical rotating plant-on-line partial discharge techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Understanding your Condition Monitoring (Ref. No.1999/117)
abstract: As reliability of strategic plant becomes more cost conscious, pressures on improved reliability and the need to reduce maintenance costs, results in the greater need for adopting effective "on-line" condition monitoring strategies. This is even more important for electrical rotating plant-generators and HV motors-which in service impose on the HV stator insulation a combination of stresses-electrical, mechanical and thermal. These can, if their effects are not identified in the early stage of initiation, result in rapid and premature failure of the HV stator insulation. This paper considers three techniques and gives examples of comparative sensitivity tests which were carried out to assess their effectiveness in detecting electrical partial discharges (PD) generated in service, in the HV stator insulation of HV motors and generators. The paper discusses radiofrequency current transformer, Rogowski coils, and permanent capacitor couplers.

articleTitle: Diagnostic monitoring of HV stator windings motors and generators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Understanding your Condition Monitoring (Ref. No.1999/117)
abstract: Reliable generation requires the early identification of defects occurring in service. This is best achieved through a planned programme of regular diagnostic testing and is particularly relevant to the electrical insulation of generators and large AC motors. The paper describes diagnostic techniques which can he applied to monitor the in-service condition of stator and rotor windings of generators and large AC motors in and out of service. The paper describes radiofrequency current transformers and partial discharge measurement.
